title: Counterfactual Fairness Through Transforming Data Orthogonal to Bias

problem.claim: Machine learning models can exhibit biased decision-making that leads to unequal treatment of different groups.

gap.claim: Existing counterfactual fairness methods remain underdeveloped for multivariate and continuous sensitive variables.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Orthogonal to Bias, a data pre-processing algorithm designed to eliminate the influence of a group of continuous sensitive variables.
The approach uses an elliptical-distribution assumption within a structural causal model and targets orthogonality between data and observed sensitive variables to achieve counterfactual fairness.
The authors introduce a sparse regularized variant to improve numerical stability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Orthogonal to Bias as a novel data pre-processing algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical evaluations on simulated and real-world datasets, including discrete and continuous sensitive-variable scenarios, are reported to demonstrate fairer outcomes without compromising predictive accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine learning models perform well across complex domains but can produce biased decisions and unequal treatment.
Existing counterfactual fairness methods do not sufficiently address multivariate and continuous sensitive variables.
The paper proposes Orthogonal to Bias, a pre-processing algorithm for removing the influence of continuous sensitive variables.
The method relies on an elliptical-distribution assumption in a structural causal model, is model-agnostic, and includes a sparse regularized variant for numerical stability.
Evaluations on simulated and real-world datasets are reported to show improved fairness without reduced predictive accuracy.

source_observation.claim: The proposed pre-processing method is described as model-agnostic and is evaluated with both discrete and continuous sensitive variables.

interpretation.claim: Separating fairness intervention from downstream model choice may broaden applicability across tasks and sensitive-variable types.

application.claim: When designing fairness interventions, consider model-agnostic pre-processing that can accommodate the sensitive-variable types present in the target setting.

exception.claim: The approach depends on an elliptical-distribution assumption within a structural causal model.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative fairness or predictive-accuracy results.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baseline methods, downstream models, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not specify the exact elliptical-distribution assumptions or the regularization procedure.
